tool.name: CellTypist
tool.description: automated cell-type annotation for single-cell transcriptomics data
tool.command: mkdir -p .cache/numba .cache/matplotlib && export NUMBA_CACHE_DIR='.cache/numba' && export MPLCONFIGDIR='.cache/matplotlib' && ln -s '$input_file' 'input.${input_file.ext}' && mkdir output && celltypist --indata 'input.${input_file.ext}' --model '$model' --outdir output --mode '$prediction.mode' #if $prediction.mode == 'prob_match' --p-thres '$prediction.probability_threshold' #end if #if str($transpose_input) == 'true' --transpose-input #end if #if $majority_voting.enabled == 'true' --majority-voting --min-prop '$majority_voting.minimum_proportion' #end if && cp output/predicted_labels.csv '$predicted_labels' && cp output/decision_matrix.csv '$decision_matrix' && cp output/probability_matrix.csv '$probability_matrix'

param.name: input_file
param.label: Single-cell expression data
param.help: Count matrix (cells by genes by default) or log1p-normalized AnnData object.

param.name: transpose_input
param.label: Genes are rows and cells are columns
param.help: Enable this for gene-by-cell tabular matrices.

tool.help:
**What it does**
CellTypist annotates cells from single-cell RNA-sequencing expression data using pretrained logistic-regression classifiers.
**Inputs**
For CSV or tabular input, supply raw counts with cells as rows and gene symbols as columns. Enable **Genes are rows and cells are columns** when the matrix is transposed. AnnData input must contain log1p-normalized expression (10,000 counts per cell) in ``.X`` or ``.raw.X``.
The **Immune All Low** model is intended for broad immune-cell populations, while **Immune All High** provides finer immune-cell resolution.
**Prediction modes**
Best match assigns the highest-scoring type to each cell. Probability match can return no label, one label, or multiple labels according to the selected probability threshold. Majority voting optionally refines labels using over-clustering.
**Outputs**
The tool returns predicted cell labels, decision scores, and cell-type probabilities as CSV datasets.
